If you are in Australia, the first question is whether a platform is licensed at home. Businesses that offer financial products or trading services to Australian retail clients generally need an Australian Financial Services (AFS) licence issued by ASIC, the Australian Securities and Investments Commission.

We could not confirm whether Turbo Hiberix holds an AFS licence or accepts clients in Australia, so treat it as unconfirmed until you have checked it yourself.

Checks for Australian traders:

  • Search the company name and any licence number on ASIC’s Financial Services Register.
  • Check ASIC’s investor alert list for the name and the website address.
  • Search the name on Scamwatch and MoneySmart for scam reports.
  • Ask whether the firm belongs to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA), the free dispute service that licensed firms dealing with retail clients are required to join.
  • Check the deposit currency. If deposits are taken in US dollars, your bank may add currency conversion charges.
  • ASIC limits the leverage retail clients can use on CFDs, so be wary of any platform that promises far higher leverage.

If you think you have been targeted by a scam, contact your bank straight away and report it to Scamwatch. This is general information, not legal or financial advice.
